title: Towards the classification of Fano 4-folds with b_2 >= 7: the case of every fixed prime divisor of type (3,0)^sm (Proposition 9.4)
author: C.~Casagrande
work: Towards the classification of Fano $4$-folds with $b_2\geq 7$
difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the 194-line case analysis on which the paper's main theorem for the case of a fixed prime divisor of type (3,0)sm rests, and no qualifying examination asks for it. Even with the paper's own prerequisites supplied as context - the definitions of fixed prime divisor, of small elementary contraction, of elementary rational contraction, of SQM, of the effective and moving cones and of the Lefschetz defect, together with the papers own announcement of the theorem it serves - the proof has to run a long reduction: it replaces the original X by a sequence of flips and divisorial elementary contractions, arranges that the resulting Y has no divisorial elementary rational contractions, reduces by SQM to the blow-up of a smooth Fano 4-fold in r distinct points, derives the relation h^0(X,-K_X)=h^0(Y,-K_Y)-15r, and then splits into the cases dim Z = 3, dim Z = 2 and dim Z = 1 for the elementary contraction of fiber type, computing in the surface cases with the classification of smooth rational surfaces, with the geometry of P^1xP^1 and of the first Hirzebruch surface, with blow-ups and flops, with the intersection theory of the resulting 4-folds, with the cone of curves and the nef and effective cones, and finally bounding h^0 of an anticanonical divisor through several auxiliary varieties W, W' and their fibrations. The proof is the longest single argument of the paper and is carried entirely by the paper's own birational machinery rather than by a textbook quote, which places the unit well above ordinary PhD qualifying examinations: H3.
